observations: Under forced scroll every box is a steering instruction; sides alternate almost box by box, producing a slalom beat every 1-2 s.
Single boxes sit on the far bank of jumps and C3 sits on a landing: the box is the landing marker.
Ice removes steering; ice groups test lane commitment before the patch, first with boxes (S1-d) then with Nitros (S3-b).
All six TNT are pre-lit timed gates that count themselves; the speed burst becomes a risk (POINT 6).
Collectible density is flat (10/5/5/7 incl. C and 1UP) while explosive density rises (0/3/6/9).
Rewards sit on the exit line of hazards (S4-b after the Nitro zone, 1UP after C1).
Count traps are lateral, not hidden: S2-b contradicts the orca-safe line, S4-e zig-zags, S4-d is missing from F2, the green ! is off the bear.
Multi-box groups run along one lane (S2-c, S3-c/d, S4-b) so one held lane collects them at speed; only S1-a and S4-e spread across lanes.
Checkpoints split boxes evenly (10/18/29 of 45) and sit in calm beats.
A missed box cannot be recovered under forced scroll: the all-box goal is four perfect segments.
openQuestions: 3 boxes unlocated (48 PS1 vs 45 mapped = N. Sane 45): possibly boxes destroyed by pre-lit TNT before arrival, Nitros under the POINT 9 callout, or a version difference.
Five plain icons are wood? (could be striped).
S4-a Nitro positions approximate; 8 is a minimum.

geometryObservations: forced scroll turns every gap into a timing-and-lane problem; what the landing holds (crate, totem, orca, checkpoint) matters more than the width
strict hazard curriculum: water pit, ice bridge, totem slalom, fallen totems, ice, seals, orcas, pre-lit TNT, ice + Nitro, Nitro field, no-stop chain, chicane, slalom slope
each idea appears soft before lethal: ice with crates then ice with Nitro; small orca opening before long and wide holes
orca holes are two-phase gates; the first leap announces the safe half; crates beyond often sit on the other half
hole size escalates in steps: small, normal, held jump from an ice edge with air steering, wide, island hop
air steering becomes the advanced move (hole 4, totems on a landing, hole B, chicane)
totems play three roles: lethal flank posts, hurdles, landing-zone hazards
edge hazards fix a 2.5-3 u centre lane on a 6-7 u road
no enemy can be attacked (no spin on the bear): seals and orcas are pure hurdles and timing gates
jump density rises and rest falls toward the end (three holes in a row, POINT 10's no-stop triple)
checkpoints sit in calm beats or on a landing
the speed burst is made risky near pre-lit TNT (POINT 6) so the player keeps the designed pace
geometryTransfer: forced-pace board run on a 7-8 m road (three 2.3 m lanes) at 12 m/s; pits 3.5-5 m (full ollie carries ~6.6 m) with a crate 1-2 m past the far lip in the landing lane
alternating orca gate: a 4-5 m pit split into halves with two hazards popping in alternation (paired crusher or firetiki offset by half a cycle); reward crate on the other half once learned
ice pre-alignment pad soft then lethal: crates first, later Nitro at both edges leaving a >=3.3 m centre lane
no-stop triple: two low walls (<=0.9 m) then a 4 m pit, touchdowns of 0.3-0.5 s (4-6 m) at cruise
hazard on the landing: a pendulum or post on one lane of each landing, side reversed after the next jump (chicane)
pace trap: a speedpad just before a timed TNT pair so the rider who takes it arrives in the blast
